help.example: Instead of building an upload tool, ask a seller to email product photos and a spreadsheet. Prepare the listings manually and send them back. This tests whether they want the result before you automate anything.
help.avoid: Avoid assuming customers will only respond to a finished product. Early users often care about the outcome, not the interface.

questions.question: Which feature would best reveal whether customers need the solution?
questions.rawQuestion: Which feature would best reveal whether customers need the solution?
questions.sourceSection: 從 Problem 到 Team：Problem、Customer、Market、Solution

help.why: One well-chosen feature can test the core need faster than a broad set. Picking it forces the team to name what it most needs to learn.
help.example: Compare candidate features: auto-filling missing specs, resizing photos, writing titles. Ask which one, if sellers used it repeatedly, would most clearly show they need help with listing data. Build only that one first.
help.avoid: Avoid picking the feature that is easiest or most fun to build. Choose the one that answers your riskiest question.

questions.question: Which validated problem does this feature solve?
questions.rawQuestion: Which validated problem does this feature solve?
questions.sourceSection: Customer Validation & Growth：訪談與訪談後的檢查
questions.sourceRange:
來源：第四至五週第 25–26、30、39–40、45、47–49 頁。

直接問顧客：


團隊檢查：

help.why: Every feature should trace back to a problem customers have confirmed in interviews. Features without that link often go unused.
help.example: Before adding photo background removal, check your interview notes. Did several sellers describe photo editing as a recurring delay, or did only one mention it in passing? Record which notes support the feature.
help.avoid: Avoid justifying a feature with a single anecdote or the team's own preference. Link it to repeated customer evidence.

questions.question: What do they need to do?
questions.rawQuestion: What do they need to do?
questions.sourceSection: Product Strategy：Problem、結果、驗證與產品範圍
questions.sourceRange:
來源：第七週第 8、11–16、19–20、26、28、31、46、52–53 頁。


直接問顧客（第 31 頁）：


最後一題在教材中明確安排於理解問題之後；不把口頭願付費等同實際付款。

help.why: Understanding the task customers must complete keeps the product focused on their job, not on screens or functions the team imagines.
help.example: Map the seller's job step by step: gather supplier details, write a title, check required fields, upload photos, publish. Watch one seller do it once and note which steps take the longest or cause rework.
help.avoid: Avoid describing what users do inside your product. Start from the work they must finish regardless of any tool.

questions.question: Which small part of the problem will we solve this time?
questions.rawQuestion: Which small part of the problem will we solve this time?（轉問句）
questions.sourceSection: Product Strategy：Problem、結果、驗證與產品範圍
questions.sourceRange:
來源：第七週第 8、11–16、19–20、26、28、31、46、52–53 頁。


直接問顧客（第 31 頁）：


最後一題在教材中明確安排於理解問題之後；不把口頭願付費等同實際付款。

help.why: Choosing a small slice of the problem makes the next test achievable and its result readable. Trying to solve everything at once blurs what you learn.
help.example: Of all listing problems, pick one, such as filling missing product specifications from supplier sheets. Leave photos and titles for later. Tell pilot sellers clearly what this round covers and what it does not.
help.avoid: Avoid a slice so broad that a failure cannot be traced to one cause.

questions.question: What is the least we need to deliver for a customer to make the first payment?
questions.rawQuestion: What is the least we need to deliver for a customer to make the first payment?
questions.sourceSection: Product Strategy：Problem、結果、驗證與產品範圍
questions.sourceRange:
來源：第七週第 8、11–16、19–20、26、28、31、46、52–53 頁。


直接問顧客（第 31 頁）：


最後一題在教材中明確安排於理解問題之後；不把口頭願付費等同實際付款。

help.why: The first payment marks the point where your offer is worth money to someone. Finding the minimum keeps scope small and learning fast.
help.example: Ask what a seller would need to receive to pay for one batch: perhaps 30 complete listings in their store's format by a set date. Deliver that manually and see whether they pay.
help.avoid: Avoid adding dashboards, accounts, or integrations before anyone has paid. These rarely decide the first purchase.

questions.question: If this were solved tomorrow, what concrete difference would it make?
questions.rawQuestion: If this were solved tomorrow, what concrete difference would it make?
questions.sourceSection: Product Strategy：Problem、結果、驗證與產品範圍
questions.sourceRange:
來源：第七週第 8、11–16、19–20、26、28、31、46、52–53 頁。


直接問顧客（第 31 頁）：


最後一題在教材中明確安排於理解問題之後；不把口頭願付費等同實際付款。

help.why: Hearing the customer describe a concrete difference shows whether solving the problem matters in their daily work. Vague answers suggest a mild problem.
help.example: Ask the seller to imagine listings were ready the moment stock arrived. Listen for specific changes: launching before a weekend sale, freeing an assistant for customer service. Ask which recent week this would have changed.
help.avoid: Avoid accepting general answers like it would be easier. Ask for a specific task, day, or result that would change.

questions.question: How does our solution address that problem?
questions.rawQuestion: How does our solution address that problem?
questions.sourceSection: Pitch 所需欄位轉問句
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第二週第 5 頁、第七週第 1 頁。這裡保留商業提問，刪除繳交及評分要求；這些題目由欄位轉寫，不是逐字問句。

help.why: Investors and customers need to see a clear link between the problem stated and the solution offered. A gap there weakens the whole pitch.
help.example: Connect each part: sellers lose launch days to missing product fields, so the service collects supplier data and returns complete listings ready to upload. Check that every claim in the link is backed by interview evidence.
help.avoid: Avoid describing the solution without naming which part of the problem it removes. The connection should be explicit.

questions.question: What product are we offering?
questions.rawQuestion: What product are we offering?
questions.sourceSection: Pitch 所需欄位轉問句
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第二週第 5 頁、第七週第 1 頁。這裡保留商業提問，刪除繳交及評分要求；這些題目由欄位轉寫，不是逐字問句。

help.why: Naming the product plainly lets others understand what they would buy or use. A fuzzy description makes feedback and decisions harder.
help.example: Write one sentence a seller could repeat: a service that turns supplier spreadsheets and photos into store-ready product listings within two days. Test it by asking a seller to explain it back in their own words.
help.avoid: Avoid describing the product as a platform or ecosystem. Say what the customer receives and in what form.

questions.question: What makes our value proposition different from existing solutions?
questions.rawQuestion: What makes our value proposition different from existing solutions?
questions.sourceSection: Pitch 所需欄位轉問句
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第二週第 5 頁、第七週第 1 頁。這裡保留商業提問，刪除繳交及評分要求；這些題目由欄位轉寫，不是逐字問句。

help.why: Customers compare you with what they use now, including spreadsheets and freelancers. Your difference must matter to them, not just sound new.
help.example: List current alternatives: doing it in-house, hiring a freelancer, generic templates. Ask sellers what bothers them about each. A possible difference is consistent output in the store's required format, but confirm it with them.
help.avoid: Avoid claiming no competition exists. Doing nothing and manual work are alternatives customers already accept.

questions.question: What is the simplest technology that lets us test the assumption?
questions.rawQuestion: What is the simplest technology that lets us test the assumption?（轉問句）
questions.sourceSection: Product Strategy：競爭、定價與建置
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第七週第 34–36、39、43、45、48–49、51 頁。明示轉問句，不把工具或技術選項當所有創業者的必答題。

help.why: Technology choices should serve the test, not the other way round. The simplest setup gets an answer sooner and costs less to throw away.
help.example: To test whether sellers want complete listings, use a shared spreadsheet, a form for photos, and manual review. Only consider custom software once sellers keep sending batches through this setup.
help.avoid: Avoid choosing a technology because the team wants to learn it. Pick what answers the assumption fastest.

questions.question: Can a rule-based system test the need before we invest in AI?
questions.rawQuestion: Can a rule-based system test the need before we invest in AI?（轉問句）
questions.sourceSection: Product Strategy：競爭、定價與建置
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第七週第 34–36、39、43、45、48–49、51 頁。明示轉問句，不把工具或技術選項當所有創業者的必答題。

help.why: Simple rules can often show whether customers want the outcome. If they do not, an AI investment would only make an unwanted product more expensive.
help.example: Write fixed rules that flag missing fields such as size, material, and weight in a seller's spreadsheet. If sellers find those flags useful and come back, then evaluate whether AI would improve the results.
help.avoid: Avoid starting with AI because it sounds impressive. First check that the underlying need exists with simpler logic.

questions.question: Can a hard-coded workflow test demand before we build full infrastructure?
questions.rawQuestion: Can a hard-coded workflow test demand before we build full infrastructure?（轉問句）
questions.sourceSection: Product Strategy：競爭、定價與建置
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第七週第 34–36、39、43、45、48–49、51 頁。明示轉問句，不把工具或技術選項當所有創業者的必答題。

help.why: A hard-coded workflow can deliver the result to a few customers quickly. It tests demand before you spend weeks on systems that may not be needed.
help.example: Build a script that converts one seller's supplier sheet into their store's import format, with their categories written directly in the code. If several sellers keep using it, generalize afterward.
help.avoid: Avoid building multi-tenant accounts, permissions, and scaling before demand appears.

questions.question: What basic design choices must remain consistent across the product?
questions.rawQuestion: What basic design choices must remain consistent across the product?（轉問句）
questions.sourceSection: Product Strategy：競爭、定價與建置
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第七週第 34–36、39、43、45、48–49、51 頁。明示轉問句，不把工具或技術選項當所有創業者的必答題。

help.why: Even an early product needs a few consistent basics so users are not confused. Agreeing on them early avoids rework as the product grows.
help.example: Agree on a few rules: the same field names everywhere, one date format, the same wording for missing information. Write them in a short shared note and check each new screen or file against it.
help.avoid: Avoid spending weeks on a full design system. Fix only the choices that would confuse users if they changed.

questions.question: Are we postponing tests, documentation, or instrumentation?
questions.rawQuestion: Are we postponing tests, documentation, or instrumentation?（轉問句）
questions.sourceSection: Product Strategy：競爭、定價與建置
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第七週第 34–36、39、43、45、48–49、51 頁。明示轉問句，不把工具或技術選項當所有創業者的必答題。

help.why: Speed matters early, but postponing everything creates hidden debt. Without basic instrumentation, you cannot see whether customers use what you built.
help.example: List what the team is skipping: automated tests, setup notes, usage tracking. Decide which to keep minimal now, such as logging every batch a seller submits, and when to revisit the rest.
help.avoid: Avoid postponing instrumentation entirely. Without it, later questions about usage and retention cannot be answered.

questions.question: Where can I find these customers today?
questions.rawQuestion: Where can I find these customers today?
questions.sourceSection: 從 Idea 到 Problem：優勢、團隊與個人
questions.sourceRange:
來源：第二週第 31、35、37、43–45 頁。


三週是教材原本的反思期間；保留來源，不預設為未來網站的固定期限。

help.why: Knowing where customers already gather tells you whether you can reach them at all. A great idea is hard to test if you cannot find anyone.
help.example: List concrete places: seller groups on social platforms, marketplace forums, local merchant meetups, suppliers who serve small shops. Visit two this week and note how many suitable sellers you could actually contact.
help.avoid: Avoid answering with online or social media in general. Name specific communities, events, or people you can approach.

questions.question: Which customer group can we reach most easily?
questions.rawQuestion: Which customer group can we reach most easily?（轉問句）
questions.sourceSection: 從 Problem 到 Team：Problem、Customer、Market、Solution

help.why: Early learning depends on talking to customers quickly. The easiest group to reach lets you run more conversations and tests in less time.
help.example: Compare segments: sellers in a forum a team member already belongs to, sellers met through a supplier contact, and sellers found by cold outreach. Record how many conversations each route produces in one week.
help.avoid: Avoid picking an easy group that does not have the problem. Reachability only helps if they fit the customer profile.

questions.question: Can we reach them soon?
questions.rawQuestion: Can we reach them soon?
questions.sourceSection: 從 Problem 到 Team：分工、組隊驗證與第一次檢查
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第三週第 47–60 頁；標記轉問句的題目由職責或 Canvas 欄位展開。

help.why: Timing affects momentum. If reaching customers takes months, the team may lose time and energy before learning anything.
help.example: Set a short window, such as the next ten days, and plan who you can contact within it. Example only: decide how many seller conversations you aim to book, then compare the plan with what actually happened.
help.avoid: Avoid planning outreach for later. Reaching customers soon is part of testing whether the plan is realistic.

questions.question: Which customer group has the highest response rate?
questions.rawQuestion: Which customer group has the highest response rate?
questions.sourceSection: Customer Validation & Growth：Growth
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第四至五週第 14–18、30、32–33 頁。除原有問句外標示轉問句。

help.why: Response rate shows which group finds the problem relevant enough to reply. It can guide where to focus limited time.
help.example: Send the same short message to two seller groups, for example clothing sellers and home goods sellers. Record how many in each group were contacted and how many replied, then compare.
help.avoid: Avoid comparing groups contacted with different messages. Change one thing at a time to see what drives replies.

questions.question: Which acquisition channel has the lowest cost?
questions.rawQuestion: Which acquisition channel has the lowest cost?
questions.sourceSection: Customer Validation & Growth：Growth
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第四至五週第 14–18、30、32–33 頁。除原有問句外標示轉問句。

help.why: Acquisition cost determines whether growth can pay for itself. Knowing it early prevents scaling a channel that loses money on each customer.
help.example: Track time and money spent per channel: forum posts, supplier referrals, small paid ads. Record how many suitable sellers each channel produced. Divide cost by that number to compare channels.
help.avoid: Avoid counting only money. Founder hours spent on a channel are also a cost.

questions.question: Which invitation message gets the highest response rate?
questions.rawQuestion: Which invitation message gets the highest response rate?
questions.sourceSection: Customer Validation & Growth：Growth
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第四至五週第 14–18、30、32–33 頁。除原有問句外標示轉問句。

help.why: The invitation is often a customer's first contact with you. Small wording changes can affect who replies, which shapes everything you learn afterward.
help.example: Write two versions: one naming the problem, such as fixing missing product details before launch, and one offering a short chat about listing work. Send each to similar sellers and record replies per version.
help.avoid: Avoid judging wording on too few messages. Wait until each version has reached enough people to compare.

questions.question: Are interviewees introducing other potential customers?
questions.rawQuestion: Are interviewees introducing other potential customers?（轉問句）
questions.sourceSection: Customer Validation & Growth：Growth
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第四至五週第 14–18、30、32–33 頁。除原有問句外標示轉問句。

help.why: When interviewees introduce peers, they are vouching for the problem's relevance. Referrals also make recruiting cheaper and faster.
help.example: At the end of each interview, ask whether they know another seller who struggles with listing preparation. Record how many offer a name, and how many introductions actually turn into conversations.
help.avoid: Avoid counting vague offers to mention it to someone. Count only introductions that lead to contact.

questions.question: What are our interview invitation response and completion rates?
questions.rawQuestion: What are our interview invitation response and completion rates?（轉問句）
questions.sourceSection: Customer Validation & Growth：Growth
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第四至五週第 14–18、30、32–33 頁。除原有問句外標示轉問句。

help.why: Response and completion rates show where recruiting breaks down. A high reply rate with low completion points to a different fix than few replies.
help.example: Track three numbers per week: invitations sent to sellers, replies received, and interviews completed. If many reply but few attend, shorten the request or offer more flexible times so attendance is easier for busy sellers.
help.avoid: Avoid tracking only completed interviews. Without the earlier counts, you cannot tell which step needs work.

questions.question: What is our customer referral rate?
questions.rawQuestion: What is our customer referral rate?（轉問句）
questions.sourceSection: Customer Validation & Growth：Growth
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第四至五週第 14–18、30、32–33 頁。除原有問句外標示轉問句。

help.why: Referral rate shows whether customers value the product enough to recommend it. It can also become a low-cost acquisition channel.
help.example: Record each new seller who arrived because an existing pilot seller recommended you. Divide by the number of active pilot sellers in the same period, and note the date of every referral.
help.avoid: Avoid relying on how much customers say they like the product. Measure the referrals that actually happen.

questions.question: What proportion of users complete the core task and return?
questions.rawQuestion: What proportion of users complete the core task and return?（轉問句）
questions.sourceSection: Customer Validation & Growth：Growth
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第四至五週第 14–18、30、32–33 頁。除原有問句外標示轉問句。

help.why: Finishing the core task once and coming back shows the first experience delivered enough value. Signups alone do not show this.
help.example: Define the core task, such as a seller uploading a supplier sheet and publishing the returned listings. Record how many new sellers do this, and how many return with another batch within a set period.
help.avoid: Avoid measuring activation by logins or account creation. These happen before the customer receives any value.

questions.question: What are the most important one or two user journeys?
questions.rawQuestion: What are the most important one or two user journeys?
questions.sourceSection: Product Strategy：Problem、結果、驗證與產品範圍
questions.sourceRange:
來源：第七週第 8、11–16、19–20、26、28、31、46、52–53 頁。


直接問顧客（第 31 頁）：


最後一題在教材中明確安排於理解問題之後；不把口頭願付費等同實際付款。

help.why: Focusing on one or two journeys keeps a small team from spreading effort thin. These paths are where the product must work well.
help.example: Pick the journey that matters most: a seller sends supplier data and receives complete listings. A second might be correcting a returned listing. Write each as steps and test them end to end.
help.avoid: Avoid listing every feature as a journey. If everything is important, nothing gets enough attention.

questions.question: When does the user first genuinely experience the product’s value?
questions.rawQuestion: When does the user first genuinely experience the product’s value?
questions.sourceSection: Product Strategy：取得、啟用、留存與量測
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第七週第 21–24、40–41 頁。以下除取得成本與首次價值原有提問外，為敘述轉問句。

help.why: Signup is not the same as receiving value.
help.example: A seller publishes a prepared listing without correcting missing information. Validate whether this is the meaningful moment for them.
help.avoid: Avoid treating account creation as proof of customer value.

questions.question: Which steps between signup and the first experience of value can we shorten?
questions.rawQuestion: Which steps between signup and the first experience of value can we shorten?（轉問句）
questions.sourceSection: Product Strategy：取得、啟用、留存與量測
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第七週第 21–24、40–41 頁。以下除取得成本與首次價值原有提問外，為敘述轉問句。

help.why: Each step before value is a chance for the user to give up. Removing unnecessary steps helps more people reach the moment that matters.
help.example: Write out every step from signup to the first ready listing: account creation, store connection, uploading files, choosing templates. Ask which steps could be skipped or done later, such as connecting the store after the first batch.
help.avoid: Avoid adding onboarding screens to explain a long process. Shorten the process itself where possible.

questions.question: Are users returning without reminders?
questions.rawQuestion: Are users returning without reminders?（轉問句）
questions.sourceSection: Customer Validation & Growth：Growth
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第四至五週第 14–18、30、32–33 頁。除原有問句外標示轉問句。

help.why: Returning voluntarily may reveal recurring value.
help.example: Observe whether the seller brings a second batch without a follow-up message. Record the event; do not infer it from satisfaction alone.
help.avoid: Avoid counting a prompted return as an unprompted one.

questions.question: Are users returning after their first trial?
questions.rawQuestion: Are users returning after their first trial?（轉問句）
questions.sourceSection: Product Strategy：取得、啟用、留存與量測
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第七週第 21–24、40–41 頁。以下除取得成本與首次價值原有提問外，為敘述轉問句。

help.why: A return visit after the first trial suggests the value was real enough to repeat. One-time use may mean curiosity, not need.
help.example: After each seller's first pilot batch, note whether they submit another one without being reminded. Record the date of the second batch, or that none arrived, for each seller in the pilot group.
help.avoid: Avoid counting returns you prompted with reminders. Those show your follow-up effort, not the customer's need.

questions.question: What do our usage patterns show?
questions.rawQuestion: What do our usage patterns show?（轉問句）
questions.sourceSection: Product Strategy：取得、啟用、留存與量測
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第七週第 21–24、40–41 頁。以下除取得成本與首次價值原有提問外，為敘述轉問句。

help.why: Usage patterns reveal how customers fit the product into their work. Timing and frequency can confirm or challenge your assumptions about the problem.
help.example: Review when sellers submit batches: only before seasonal sales, or steadily each week? Plot submission dates per seller. A seasonal pattern may change how you price the service and plan support capacity.
help.avoid: Avoid looking only at totals. Averages can hide that a few heavy users carry most of the activity.

questions.question: If users are leaving, what should we reconsider about the problem, requirements, or value proposition?
questions.rawQuestion: If users are leaving, what should we reconsider about the problem, requirements, or value proposition?（轉問句）
questions.sourceSection: Product Strategy：取得、啟用、留存與量測
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第七週第 21–24、40–41 頁。以下除取得成本與首次價值原有提問外，為敘述轉問句。

help.why: When users leave, the cause may lie upstream in the problem itself, not in a missing feature. Looking back helps avoid fixing the wrong thing.
help.example: If sellers stop after one batch, ask what changed. Perhaps listing is rare for them, or missing data comes from suppliers you cannot reach. Revisit your interview notes and decide which assumption to retest.
help.avoid: Avoid responding to churn by adding features right away. First check whether the original problem was frequent and painful.

questions.question: What is our retention rate?
questions.rawQuestion: What is our retention rate?
questions.sourceSection: Product Strategy：取得、啟用、留存與量測
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第七週第 21–24、40–41 頁。以下除取得成本與首次價值原有提問外，為敘述轉問句。

help.why: Retention rate summarizes whether customers keep getting value over time. It is one of the clearest signals that the product solves a recurring problem.
help.example: Group sellers by the month they started. Record what share submitted at least one batch in each following month. Example only: decide in advance which period you will treat as the retention window.
help.avoid: Avoid calculating retention without a fixed time window. Without one, the number cannot be compared across groups.

questions.question: What are our trial and paid conversion rates?
questions.rawQuestion: What are our trial and paid conversion rates?（轉問句）
questions.sourceSection: Customer Validation & Growth：Growth
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第四至五週第 14–18、30、32–33 頁。除原有問句外標示轉問句。

help.why: Trial and paid conversion show where interest turns into commitment. They help you see whether the offer or the trial experience needs work.
help.example: Record how many sellers start a trial, how many complete it, and how many then pay for a batch. Track these as separate counts so you can see which step loses the most people.
help.avoid: Avoid combining trial and paid conversion into one figure. Each points to a different problem to fix.

questions.question: Where do users click?
questions.rawQuestion: Where do users click?
questions.sourceSection: Product Strategy：取得、啟用、留存與量測
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第七週第 21–24、40–41 頁。以下除取得成本與首次價值原有提問外，為敘述轉問句。

help.why: Click data shows where users focus and where they get confused. It can reveal problems that users never mention in interviews.
help.example: Log clicks on the main screens of the listing tool, such as upload, preview, and edit field. Review whether sellers repeatedly click something that is not interactive, or skip the preview entirely.
help.avoid: Avoid tracking every click without a question in mind. Decide what you want to learn before adding tracking.

questions.question: Which features do they use?
questions.rawQuestion: Which features do they use?
questions.sourceSection: Product Strategy：取得、啟用、留存與量測
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第七週第 21–24、40–41 頁。以下除取得成本與首次價值原有提問外，為敘述轉問句。

help.why: Knowing which features are used shows where customers find value. It helps you decide what to improve and what to stop maintaining.
help.example: Record each time a seller uses a feature: bulk upload, missing-field flags, title suggestions. After a few weeks, list which features each seller used at least once, and which ones only appeared in demos.
help.avoid: Avoid relying on what users say they use. Actual usage often differs from their own description.

questions.question: At which step do they leave?
questions.rawQuestion: At which step do they leave?
questions.sourceSection: Product Strategy：取得、啟用、留存與量測
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第七週第 21–24、40–41 頁。以下除取得成本與首次價值原有提問外，為敘述轉問句。

help.why: The step where users drop out shows where your process fails them. It tells you where to look first when fixing the flow.
help.example: Log each step of the main journey: upload started, file accepted, listings previewed, listings exported. Count how many sellers reach each step and find the biggest drop between two of them.
help.avoid: Avoid guessing the drop-off point from complaints. Measure each step so the data points to the real gap.

questions.question: Which features are heavily adopted?
questions.rawQuestion: Which features are heavily adopted?
questions.sourceSection: Product Strategy：取得、啟用、留存與量測
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第七週第 21–24、40–41 頁。以下除取得成本與首次價值原有提問外，為敘述轉問句。

help.why: Heavily adopted features often point to the core value. They show what to protect and strengthen as the product changes.
help.example: Rank features by how many active sellers use them each week. If most use missing-field flags but few use title suggestions, consider making the flags the center of the product.
help.avoid: Avoid confusing heavy adoption with a single power user. Check how many different customers use the feature.

questions.question: Which features does nobody use?
questions.rawQuestion: Which features does nobody use?
questions.sourceSection: Product Strategy：取得、啟用、留存與量測
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第七週第 21–24、40–41 頁。以下除取得成本與首次價值原有提問外，為敘述轉問句。

help.why: Unused features cost maintenance and clutter the product. Finding them helps you remove distractions and question the assumptions behind them.
help.example: After a set period, list features with no use by any active seller, such as a template library nobody opened. Ask a few sellers whether they knew it existed before deciding to remove it.
help.avoid: Avoid keeping unused features because effort went into building them. Past effort is not a reason to keep them.

questions.question: What is our conversion rate?
questions.rawQuestion: What is our conversion rate?
questions.sourceSection: Product Strategy：取得、啟用、留存與量測
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第七週第 21–24、40–41 頁。以下除取得成本與首次價值原有提問外，為敘述轉問句。

help.why: Conversion rate shows how well each stage moves people toward value or payment. It makes the funnel measurable instead of anecdotal.
help.example: Define the stages first, such as visited the page, requested a sample, received listings, paid. Record the counts at each stage for the same group of sellers over the same period.
help.avoid: Avoid quoting a conversion rate without saying which two stages it connects. The number means nothing without its definition.

questions.question: What is our error rate?
questions.rawQuestion: What is our error rate?
questions.sourceSection: Product Strategy：取得、啟用、留存與量測
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第七週第 21–24、40–41 頁。以下除取得成本與首次價值原有提問外，為敘述轉問句。

help.why: Errors break trust quickly, especially for sellers publishing to a live store. Tracking them shows whether quality issues are driving users away.
help.example: Log every failed upload, rejected export, and listing a seller had to correct by hand. Record the number of errors per batch, and review the most common causes each week.
help.avoid: Avoid counting only system crashes. Wrong or incomplete listing data is also an error from the seller's view.

questions.question: How will we earn revenue and grow?
questions.rawQuestion: How will we earn revenue and grow?
questions.sourceSection: 從 Problem 到 Team：商業模式
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第三週第 3、9、13–14 頁。標有「轉問句」者從原欄位展開。

help.why: Revenue and growth are linked. A way of earning money that cannot expand with more customers limits how far the business can go.
help.example: Suppose sellers pay per prepared listing. Write down how revenue would rise: more listings from the same seller, more sellers, or both. Then note which of those paths you have actually seen a seller take so far.
help.avoid: Avoid answering with a revenue target alone, without describing the customer behavior that would produce it.

questions.question: Is our revenue repeatable?
questions.rawQuestion: Is our revenue repeatable?
questions.sourceSection: 從 Problem 到 Team：商業模式
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第三週第 3、9、13–14 頁。標有「轉問句」者從原欄位展開。

help.why: One-time payments force you to find new buyers every month. Repeatable revenue shows whether customers come back to pay again for the same value.
help.example: Record how many pilot sellers pay for a second batch of listings without being chased. Example only: decide in advance how many repeat purchases within two months would count as a repeatable pattern for you.
help.avoid: Avoid counting a seller's promise to keep using the service as repeat revenue before a second payment happens.

questions.question: How do we capture the value?
questions.rawQuestion: How do we capture the value?
questions.sourceSection: Product Strategy：競爭、定價與建置
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第七週第 34–36、39、43、45、48–49、51 頁。明示轉問句，不把工具或技術選項當所有創業者的必答題。

help.why: Creating value for customers does not guarantee you receive part of it. Capture depends on who pays, when, and for which outcome.
help.example: A seller saves preparation time on each launch. Decide whether you charge when listings are delivered, monthly for access, or per product published. Ask a pilot seller which moment feels like the right point to pay.
help.avoid: Avoid assuming customers will pay simply because the product saves them effort; check where payment naturally fits.

questions.question: Does our free version provide value on its own?
questions.rawQuestion: Does our free version provide value on its own?（轉問句）
questions.sourceSection: Product Strategy：競爭、定價與建置
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第七週第 34–36、39、43、45、48–49、51 頁。明示轉問句，不把工具或技術選項當所有創業者的必答題。

help.why: A free tier only attracts and keeps users if it solves something real. An empty free version teaches nothing and converts nobody.
help.example: Imagine a free checker that flags missing fields in a seller's product spreadsheet. Watch whether sellers use it for a real launch and fix the flagged fields, even if they never upgrade.
help.avoid: Avoid offering a free version that is only a locked demo with no outcome a seller can use.

questions.question: What gives free users a clear reason to upgrade?
questions.rawQuestion: What gives free users a clear reason to upgrade?（轉問句）
questions.sourceSection: Product Strategy：競爭、定價與建置
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第七週第 34–36、39、43、45、48–49、51 頁。明示轉問句，不把工具或技術選項當所有創業者的必答題。

help.why: Free users stay free unless the paid version solves a problem the free one leaves open. The upgrade trigger must be concrete.
help.example: A free checker finds missing fields, but the paid plan fills them in and formats titles. Record the moment sellers ask for the fix rather than the warning; that request marks a possible upgrade point.
help.avoid: Avoid relying on usage limits alone when free users never reach them or do not feel the limit.

questions.question: Do we have enough traffic to support an advertising model?
questions.rawQuestion: Do we have enough traffic to support an advertising model?（轉問句）
questions.sourceSection: Product Strategy：競爭、定價與建置
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第七週第 34–36、39、43、45、48–49、51 頁。明示轉問句，不把工具或技術選項當所有創業者的必答題。

help.why: Advertising pays only at large audience scale. A small, focused tool may never reach the traffic needed for ads to cover costs.
help.example: Estimate how many seller visits per month your listing tool currently gets, then compare that to what an advertiser would need. If the gap is very large, consider direct payment from sellers instead.
help.avoid: Avoid choosing ads as a default model because charging users feels uncomfortable.

questions.question: Does the product provide ongoing value that justifies a subscription?
questions.rawQuestion: Does the product provide ongoing value that justifies a subscription?（轉問句）
questions.sourceSection: Product Strategy：競爭、定價與建置
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第七週第 34–36、39、43、45、48–49、51 頁。明示轉問句，不把工具或技術選項當所有創業者的必答題。

help.why: A subscription asks customers to pay every month. That only feels fair if they receive value every month, not once.
help.example: Check whether sellers launch new products often enough to need help monthly. Ask a seller to show their launch dates over the past few months and see whether the need repeats on a regular rhythm.
help.avoid: Avoid adopting a subscription because recurring revenue looks attractive, when the customer's need is occasional.

questions.question: Does the value occur only once?
questions.rawQuestion: Does the value occur only once?（轉問句）
questions.sourceSection: Product Strategy：競爭、定價與建置
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第七週第 34–36、39、43、45、48–49、51 頁。明示轉問句，不把工具或技術選項當所有創業者的必答題。

help.why: If customers need you only once, a subscription will churn quickly and a one-time or per-project price may fit better.
help.example: A seller might need a full catalog cleanup once, then only small updates afterward. Track whether pilot sellers return after the first cleanup, and price the first job differently from the follow-up work if needed.
help.avoid: Avoid treating a large first project as proof of ongoing demand from the same seller.

questions.question: What pricing unit makes sense in the customer’s business?
questions.rawQuestion: What pricing unit makes sense in the customer’s business?（轉問句）
questions.sourceSection: Product Strategy：競爭、定價與建置
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第七週第 34–36、39、43、45、48–49、51 頁。明示轉問句，不把工具或技術選項當所有創業者的必答題。

help.why: Pricing is easier to understand when it matches the work customers recognize.
help.example: Compare paying per listing with paying for model tokens. Test which unit the seller can connect to a useful outcome.
help.avoid: Avoid charging in technical units customers cannot relate to value.

questions.question: What is our business model?
questions.rawQuestion: What is our business model?
questions.sourceSection: Pitch 所需欄位轉問句
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第二週第 5 頁、第七週第 1 頁。這裡保留商業提問，刪除繳交及評分要求；這些題目由欄位轉寫，不是逐字問句。

help.why: Investors and teammates need a short statement of who pays, for what, and how the money arrives. Without it, plans drift.
help.example: One possible statement: small sellers pay a fee per batch of prepared listings, delivered before each launch. Write your version in one sentence, then mark which parts are tested and which are still assumptions.
help.avoid: Avoid listing several possible models at once without choosing the one you are testing now.

questions.question: What are our revenue sources and charging methods?
questions.rawQuestion: What are our revenue sources and charging methods?
questions.sourceSection: Pitch 所需欄位轉問句
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第二週第 5 頁、第七週第 1 頁。這裡保留商業提問，刪除繳交及評分要求；這些題目由欄位轉寫，不是逐字問句。

help.why: Naming each revenue source and how it is charged reveals whether pricing matches the customer's work and how cash actually arrives.
help.example: List each source separately, such as per-listing fees, a setup fee for catalog cleanup, or a monthly plan. For each one, note who pays, the pricing unit, and whether any seller has paid that way yet.
help.avoid: Avoid mixing planned revenue sources with ones customers have actually paid for in the same list.

questions.question: Are our gross margins high enough?
questions.rawQuestion: Are our gross margins high enough?
questions.sourceSection: 從 Problem 到 Team：商業模式
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第三週第 3、9、13–14 頁。標有「轉問句」者從原欄位展開。

help.why: Gross margin shows what is left after the direct cost of serving each customer. Thin margins leave little room to grow.
help.example: For one batch of listings, record the hours your team spends on manual fixes plus any tool or model costs. Compare that total with the price charged and see how much remains for the business.
help.avoid: Avoid ignoring manual work hidden behind the product when calculating the cost of delivering each batch.

questions.question: Do our unit economics work?
questions.rawQuestion: Do our unit economics work?
questions.sourceSection: 從 Problem 到 Team：商業模式
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第三週第 3、9、13–14 頁。標有「轉問句」者從原欄位展開。

help.why: Unit economics test whether a single customer is profitable. If one does not work, adding more customers only multiplies losses.
help.example: Pick one pilot seller. Add up what it cost to find them, the cost of serving their listings, and what they paid. Example only: decide what profit per seller you would need before scaling outreach.
help.avoid: Avoid hoping scale will fix negative unit economics without knowing which cost will actually fall.

questions.question: What does it cost to acquire a customer?
questions.rawQuestion: What does it cost to acquire a customer?（轉問句）
questions.sourceSection: 從 Problem 到 Team：商業模式
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第三週第 3、9、13–14 頁。標有「轉問句」者從原欄位展開。

help.why: Knowing acquisition cost tells you how much you can afford to spend on finding customers before each new customer becomes a loss.
help.example: Track the hours and money spent on outreach to sellers, such as messages, community posts, and calls, then divide by the number who became paying customers. Record the channel used for each customer.
help.avoid: Avoid leaving founder time out of acquisition cost because no money was spent directly.

questions.question: What is the lifetime value of a customer?
questions.rawQuestion: What is the lifetime value of a customer?（轉問句）
questions.sourceSection: 從 Problem 到 Team：商業模式
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第三週第 3、9、13–14 頁。標有「轉問句」者從原欄位展開。

help.why: Lifetime value estimates how much a customer brings in before leaving. It sets the ceiling on what acquisition can sensibly cost.
help.example: With early sellers, you cannot observe a full lifetime yet. Record how many batches each seller has bought and how long they have stayed, then state any lifetime estimate clearly as an assumption to revisit.
help.avoid: Avoid projecting a multi-year lifetime from a few months of data and presenting it as known.

questions.question: How long does it take to recover our customer acquisition cost?
questions.rawQuestion: How long does it take to recover our customer acquisition cost?（轉問句）
questions.sourceSection: 從 Problem 到 Team：商業模式
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第三週第 3、9、13–14 頁。標有「轉問句」者從原欄位展開。

help.why: The payback period shows how long your cash is tied up in each new customer. Long payback strains a small team's runway.
help.example: Suppose finding one seller cost a certain amount of outreach time and money. Record how many months of that seller's payments it takes to cover that cost, and compare it with how long your cash can last.
help.avoid: Avoid calculating payback with revenue instead of margin, which makes recovery look faster than it is.

questions.question: What are our gross margin and customer retention rate?
questions.rawQuestion: What are our gross margin and customer retention rate?（轉問句）
questions.sourceSection: 從 Problem 到 Team：商業模式
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第三週第 3、9、13–14 頁。標有「轉問句」者從原欄位展開。

help.why: Margin and retention together show whether each customer earns money and stays long enough for that money to add up.
help.example: For each pilot seller, record the margin on every batch and whether they returned the next month. Put the two side by side; a high margin with sellers who leave quickly tells a different story than steady returns.
help.avoid: Avoid reporting one of the two numbers alone when the other one is weak.

questions.question: How much does it cost to acquire one user?
questions.rawQuestion: How much does it cost to acquire one user?
questions.sourceSection: Product Strategy：取得、啟用、留存與量測
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第七週第 21–24、40–41 頁。以下除取得成本與首次價值原有提問外，為敘述轉問句。

help.why: Within product strategy, the cost of one user shows which acquisition channel deserves more effort and which should stop.
help.example: Compare channels for reaching sellers, such as seller forums, marketplace groups, and referrals from existing pilots. For each, record the time and money spent and how many sellers signed up and completed a first listing.
help.avoid: Avoid averaging all channels into one number, which hides the channel that is actually working.

questions.question: Is customer acquisition cost lower than customer value?
questions.rawQuestion: Is customer acquisition cost lower than customer value?（轉問句）
questions.sourceSection: Product Strategy：取得、啟用、留存與量測
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第七週第 21–24、40–41 頁。以下除取得成本與首次價值原有提問外，為敘述轉問句。

help.why: If acquiring a customer costs more than that customer brings in, every new signup makes the business weaker.
help.example: Place two figures next to each other for your seller pilots: what it cost to bring each seller in, and the margin they have produced so far. Mark which sellers have already covered their own acquisition cost.
help.avoid: Avoid comparing acquisition cost with an optimistic future value instead of the value customers have produced.

questions.question: What are our revenue, costs, and unit economics?
questions.rawQuestion: What are our revenue, costs, and unit economics?（轉問句）
questions.sourceSection: Product Strategy：取得、啟用、留存與量測
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第七週第 21–24、40–41 頁。以下除取得成本與首次價值原有提問外，為敘述轉問句。

help.why: Seeing revenue, costs, and per-customer economics on one page reveals whether the current activity can support the team at all.
help.example: Build a simple monthly table: revenue from listing batches, direct delivery costs, outreach costs, and fixed costs such as tools. Add a row for profit per seller. Keep tested figures and assumptions in separate columns.
help.avoid: Avoid presenting a polished spreadsheet where assumptions and recorded figures cannot be told apart.

questions.question: What are our average revenue per user and monthly recurring revenue growth?
questions.rawQuestion: What are our average revenue per user and monthly recurring revenue growth?（轉問句）
questions.sourceSection: Product Strategy：取得、啟用、留存與量測
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第七週第 21–24、40–41 頁。以下除取得成本與首次價值原有提問外，為敘述轉問句。

help.why: Average revenue per user and recurring revenue growth show whether sellers spend more over time and whether the base keeps expanding.
help.example: Each month, record total recurring revenue from sellers and divide it by active sellers. Note whether growth comes from new sellers joining or existing sellers sending larger batches, since each points to a different next step.
help.avoid: Avoid counting one-time cleanup fees as monthly recurring revenue, which inflates the growth line.

questions.question: What are our financial projections?
questions.rawQuestion: What are our financial projections?
questions.sourceSection: Pitch 所需欄位轉問句
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第二週第 5 頁、第七週第 1 頁。這裡保留商業提問，刪除繳交及評分要求；這些題目由欄位轉寫，不是逐字問句。

help.why: Projections show how you think the business will grow and what must be true for that to happen. The assumptions matter most.
help.example: Project seller count, price per batch, batches per month, and costs for the next year. Example only: choose a conservative and an optimistic case. Beside each line, write the assumption behind it and what would test it.
help.avoid: Avoid a single steep curve with no stated assumptions behind each number.

questions.question: Does growth depend on adding more people?
questions.rawQuestion: Does growth depend on adding more people?
questions.sourceSection: 從 Problem 到 Team：商業模式
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第三週第 3、9、13–14 頁。標有「轉問句」者從原欄位展開。

help.why: If each new customer needs more staff, costs rise with revenue and the business struggles to scale beyond the team's capacity.
help.example: Today the team fixes listings by hand. Record how many hours one seller's batch takes. If doubling sellers would need roughly double the hours, growth still depends on people and automation is the next question.
help.avoid: Avoid assuming software will remove manual work later without measuring how much manual work exists now.

questions.question: Does growth come from replicating the product, network effects, or adding people and inventory?
questions.rawQuestion: Does growth come from replicating the product, network effects, or adding people and inventory?
questions.sourceSection: 從 Problem 到 Team：商業模式
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第三週第 3、9、13–14 頁。標有「轉問句」者從原欄位展開。

help.why: The source of growth determines its cost. Copying software is cheap, network effects compound, but people and inventory grow costs too.
help.example: For the listing service, mark which parts copy at almost no cost, such as a field checker, and which need a person, such as rewriting titles. Note whether sellers referring other sellers could create any network effect.
help.avoid: Avoid claiming network effects when customers do not actually benefit from each other's participation.

questions.question: Does this activity bring us closer to customers, validation, usage, or revenue?
questions.rawQuestion: Does this activity bring us closer to customers, validation, usage, or revenue?
questions.sourceSection: Customer Validation & Growth：Growth
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第四至五週第 14–18、30、32–33 頁。除原有問句外標示轉問句。

help.why: Small teams easily fill weeks with busy work. This check keeps effort tied to customers, evidence, usage, or revenue.
help.example: Before redesigning the dashboard, ask which of the four it moves. Booking three more seller calls brings you closer to customers; polishing a page nobody visits may not. Write the answer next to each planned task.
help.avoid: Avoid treating tasks that feel productive, like tool setup or branding, as progress without that link.

questions.question: Are we getting closer to a sustainable business model?
questions.rawQuestion: Are we getting closer to a sustainable business model?
questions.sourceSection: Customer Validation & Growth：Growth
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第四至五週第 14–18、30、32–33 頁。除原有問句外標示轉問句。

help.why: Growth means little if each month still depends on effort that cannot last. This question checks direction, not just activity.
help.example: Compare this month with last month for your seller pilots: are more sellers paying, is delivery taking fewer hours per batch, and are fewer sellers leaving? Record the change in each rather than relying on a general feeling.
help.avoid: Avoid judging progress by signups or attention while payment and delivery cost stay unchanged.

questions.question: Can we repeat the way we acquire and serve customers?
questions.rawQuestion: Can we repeat the way we acquire and serve customers?（轉問句）
questions.sourceSection: Customer Validation & Growth：Growth
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第四至五週第 14–18、30、32–33 頁。除原有問句外標示轉問句。

help.why: Growth needs a process that works again, not a lucky win. Repeatability shows whether the first customers can be followed by more.
help.example: Write down how each pilot seller was found, onboarded, and served. If the next three sellers can come through the same steps with similar effort, the process may be repeatable. Note where each one differed.
help.avoid: Avoid assuming a deal won through a personal connection can be repeated with strangers.

questions.question: Which effective practices can the whole team reuse?
questions.rawQuestion: Which effective practices can the whole team reuse?（轉問句）
questions.sourceSection: Customer Validation & Growth：Growth
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第四至五週第 14–18、30、32–33 頁。除原有問句外標示轉問句。

help.why: When one teammate finds something that works, the team grows faster if others can repeat it instead of rediscovering it.
help.example: One founder may have a message that gets sellers to book calls. Write the steps and the exact wording down, let another teammate use it for a week, and record whether bookings follow.
help.avoid: Avoid keeping effective practices in one person's head, where nobody else can use or check them.

questions.question: Where should we invest our limited time, people, and attention?
questions.rawQuestion: Where should we invest our limited time, people, and attention?（轉問句）
questions.sourceSection: Customer Validation & Growth：Growth
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第四至五週第 14–18、30、32–33 頁。除原有問句外標示轉問句。

help.why: A small team cannot pursue every channel and feature. Choosing where effort goes is often the most important growth decision.
help.example: List current efforts, such as seller outreach, building automated title rewriting, and running social posts. For each, record time spent last week and what it produced. Keep the one or two with clearer results and pause the rest.
help.avoid: Avoid spreading effort evenly across everything to avoid the discomfort of stopping something.

questions.question: Do I have a genuine interest in this problem?
questions.rawQuestion: Do I have a genuine interest in this problem?
questions.sourceSection: 從 Idea 到 Problem：優勢、團隊與個人
questions.sourceRange:
來源：第二週第 31、35、37、43–45 頁。


三週是教材原本的反思期間；保留來源，不預設為未來網站的固定期限。

help.why: Early work on a problem is slow and often disappointing. Real interest is what keeps you reading, asking, and returning to it when nothing is working yet.
help.example: Suppose a founder of the listing-data team notices she reads seller forum threads about messy product spreadsheets in her free time. Write down two moments in the past month when you chose to spend time on this problem without anyone asking you to.
help.avoid: Avoid answering from how exciting the market sounds. Interest shows up in what you already do, not what you plan to do.

questions.question: Am I willing to spend a year studying this field?
questions.rawQuestion: Am I willing to spend a year studying this field?
questions.sourceSection: 從 Idea 到 Problem：優勢、團隊與個人
questions.sourceRange:
來源：第二週第 31、35、37、43–45 頁。


三週是教材原本的反思期間；保留來源，不預設為未來網站的固定期限。

help.why: Understanding a field well enough to spot a real opportunity takes time. A year of study is a test of whether you will stay long enough to learn it.
help.example: For the listing-data venture, a year might mean learning marketplace listing rules, supplier data formats, and how small sellers plan launches. List the topics you would study and estimate the hours per week you would honestly give them.
help.avoid: Avoid saying yes without picturing the dull parts, such as reading platform policy pages and comparing spreadsheet templates.

questions.question: Am I willing to talk to strangers to validate this problem?
questions.rawQuestion: Am I willing to talk to strangers to validate this problem?
questions.sourceSection: 從 Idea 到 Problem：優勢、團隊與個人
questions.sourceRange:
來源：第二週第 31、35、37、43–45 頁。


三週是教材原本的反思期間；保留來源，不預設為未來網站的固定期限。

help.why: Most of what you learn about a problem comes from people you do not know yet. If talking to strangers feels impossible, the problem cannot be checked.
help.example: One founder could try sending short messages to five small sellers she has never met, asking about their last product launch. Notice how it feels to send them and whether you would repeat it next week.
help.avoid: Avoid planning to rely only on friends and former colleagues, who tend to be polite rather than accurate.

questions.question: Would I still care about this problem if the solution changed?
questions.rawQuestion: Would I still care about this problem if the solution changed?
questions.sourceSection: 從 Idea 到 Problem：優勢、團隊與個人
questions.sourceRange:
來源：第二週第 31、35、37、43–45 頁。


三週是教材原本的反思期間；保留來源，不預設為未來網站的固定期限。

help.why: Your first solution will probably change. Caring about the problem itself, not your favorite feature, is what lets you keep going after the first idea fails.
help.example: Imagine the team learns that sellers do not want an automated listing tool, but would accept a checklist service. Ask yourself whether you would still want to help these sellers with missing product fields in that case.
help.avoid: Avoid treating attachment to a specific app, design, or technology as attachment to the problem.

questions.question: What am I good at?
questions.rawQuestion: What am I good at?
questions.sourceSection: 從 Idea 到 Problem：優勢、團隊與個人
questions.sourceRange:
來源：第二週第 31、35、37、43–45 頁。


三週是教材原本的反思期間；保留來源，不預設為未來網站的固定期限。

help.why: Your strengths shape which problems you can study well and which work you can carry yourself. Knowing them early helps you choose a fitting role.
help.example: In the listing-data team, one person may be good at cleaning spreadsheets, another at writing clear product copy, and another at calming stressed customers. Ask two people who have worked with you what they would hand you first.
help.avoid: Avoid listing only job titles or tools. Describe what you have actually done well and could do again.

questions.question: Which problem areas do I care about?
questions.rawQuestion: Which problem areas do I care about?
questions.sourceSection: 從 Idea 到 Problem：優勢、團隊與個人
questions.sourceRange:
來源：第二週第 31、35、37、43–45 頁。


三週是教材原本的反思期間；保留來源，不預設為未來網站的固定期限。

help.why: Starting from areas you already care about gives you a wider list to choose from, before you lock onto a single idea too early.
help.example: A founder might list small online retail, supplier communication, and product photography as areas she keeps noticing. Write three to five areas, then add one recent situation in each where you saw someone struggle.
help.avoid: Avoid naming only areas that sound popular or fundable when you have no personal pull toward them.

questions.question: Am I interested in a real pain point, or just an interesting idea?
questions.rawQuestion: Am I interested in a real pain point, or just an interesting idea?
questions.sourceSection: 從 Idea 到 Problem：優勢、團隊與個人
questions.sourceRange:
來源：第二週第 31、35、37、43–45 頁。


三週是教材原本的反思期間；保留來源，不預設為未來網站的固定期限。

help.why: An interesting idea can feel exciting while solving nothing anyone urgently needs. Separating the two keeps you from building something only you find clever.
help.example: An AI tool that writes poetic product titles may be an interesting idea. A seller delaying a launch because supplier specs are missing is a pain point. Note which one you could describe with a real past event.
help.avoid: Avoid judging by how much you enjoy explaining the idea. Enjoyment of the concept is not evidence of pain.

questions.question: What am I most afraid of right now?
questions.rawQuestion: What am I most afraid of right now?
questions.sourceSection: 從 Idea 到 Problem：優勢、團隊與個人
questions.sourceRange:
來源：第二週第 31、35、37、43–45 頁。


三週是教材原本的反思期間；保留來源，不預設為未來網站的固定期限。

help.why: Fear quietly shapes decisions, such as avoiding interviews or delaying a test. Naming it lets the team plan around it instead of being steered by it.
help.example: A founder in the listing-data team might admit she fears being rejected by sellers, or losing savings, or looking foolish to former colleagues. Write the fear down and one small step that would make it easier to face this week.
help.avoid: Avoid answering that you are not afraid of anything. That usually means the fear has not been looked at yet.

questions.question: Can I treat failure as information rather than a personal defeat?
questions.rawQuestion: Can I treat failure as information rather than a personal defeat?
questions.sourceSection: 從 Idea 到 Problem：優勢、團隊與個人
questions.sourceRange:
來源：第二週第 31、35、37、43–45 頁。


三週是教材原本的反思期間；保留來源，不預設為未來網站的固定期限。

help.why: Many early tests will not go the way you hope. Seeing failure as information keeps you learning instead of hiding results or quitting too early.
help.example: Suppose ten sellers decline a pilot. A founder who treats this as information would ask what they said, sort the reasons, and change the next test. Recall a recent setback and note what you learned from it.
help.avoid: Avoid promising to stay calm about failure without checking how you reacted to a real setback before.

questions.question: In which fields can I understand problems, find customers, or access data more easily than most people?
questions.rawQuestion: In which fields can I understand problems, find customers, or access data more easily than most people?
questions.sourceSection: 從 Problem 到 Team：Problem、Customer、Market、Solution

help.why: An unfair head start in understanding a field, reaching its customers, or seeing its data makes early learning faster and cheaper than for outsiders.
help.example: A founder who once ran a small online shop may know seller groups, understand marketplace upload rules, and still have old listing spreadsheets. List the fields where you could contact ten relevant people within a week.
help.avoid: Avoid claiming access you have not used yet. Test whether those contacts actually reply before counting them as an advantage.

questions.question: Do I genuinely care about this problem?
questions.rawQuestion: Do I genuinely care about this problem?
questions.sourceSection: 從 Problem 到 Team：合作
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第三週第 44–48 頁。

help.why: When forming a team, each person's care for the problem decides how much effort they will give. This check is personal before it becomes shared.
help.example: Before agreeing to join the listing-data team, each founder could write one sentence on why seller listing problems matter to them personally, then read the sentences aloud. Notice whose answer is specific and whose is vague.
help.avoid: Avoid answering yes because the other founders are enthusiastic. Their care does not count as yours.

questions.question: Am I willing to spend time understanding these customers?
questions.rawQuestion: Am I willing to spend time understanding these customers?
questions.sourceSection: 從 Problem 到 Team：合作
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第三週第 44–48 頁。

help.why: A team can only serve customers it understands. Willingness to learn about these specific customers matters more than general interest in startups.
help.example: For small e-commerce sellers, understanding might mean watching someone prepare a batch of listings, joining seller communities, and reading their complaints about platforms. Each person can name how many hours they would spend on this in the next two weeks.
help.avoid: Avoid treating customer understanding as one teammate's job while others only build or plan.

questions.question: Am I willing to interview strangers?
questions.rawQuestion: Am I willing to interview strangers?
questions.sourceSection: 從 Problem 到 Team：合作
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第三週第 44–48 頁。

help.why: Interviews are a shared team job, not a task for the most outgoing person. Each member needs to decide whether they will take part.
help.example: In the listing-data team, each founder could commit to running at least two seller interviews, then compare notes. Someone uncomfortable can start by taking notes in another person's interview before leading their own.
help.avoid: Avoid letting one teammate do every interview while the rest only hear a summary of what sellers said.

questions.question: Will I stay if our original solution is rejected?
questions.rawQuestion: Will I stay if our original solution is rejected?
questions.sourceSection: 從 Problem 到 Team：合作
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第三週第 44–48 頁。

help.why: Teams often form around one solution. If that solution is rejected, members who joined only for it may leave and stall the work.
help.example: Suppose sellers reject the planned listing editor but describe a different problem with supplier data. Each founder can write whether they would stay to work on that, and what would make them leave.
help.avoid: Avoid answering for the team as a whole. Each person states their own answer, privately first if needed.

questions.question: Do I believe this problem is worth investigating?
questions.rawQuestion: Do I believe this problem is worth investigating?
questions.sourceSection: 從 Problem 到 Team：合作
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第三週第 44–48 頁。

help.why: Investigating a problem costs weeks of effort. Believing it deserves that effort is what makes each member willing to do the unglamorous research.
help.example: A founder could explain to teammates why missing product data for small sellers seems worth three weeks of investigation, and what finding would make her stop. Compare whether each person's reason holds up.
help.avoid: Avoid confusing belief that the problem is worth investigating with belief that it is already solved or confirmed.

questions.question: Why is this founder or team suited to this problem?
questions.rawQuestion: Why is this founder or team suited to this problem?（由 Founder fit 欄位轉問句）
questions.editorialNote: （由 Founder fit 欄位轉問句）
questions.sourceSection: 從 Problem 到 Team：分工、組隊驗證與第一次檢查
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第三週第 47–60 頁；標記轉問句的題目由職責或 Canvas 欄位展開。

help.why: Investors, partners, and early customers want to know why this team, rather than another, can understand and solve this problem well.
help.example: For the listing-data venture, a fit statement might combine one founder's years running a small shop, an engineer who has built spreadsheet import tools, and access to seller groups. Attach evidence for each claim, such as past work or contacts.
help.avoid: Avoid generic traits like passion or hard work that any team could claim without evidence.

questions.question: What contribution can I make?
questions.rawQuestion: What contribution can I make?
questions.sourceSection: 從 Problem 到 Team：分工、組隊驗證與第一次檢查
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第三週第 47–60 頁；標記轉問句的題目由職責或 Canvas 欄位展開。

help.why: Team fit includes concrete work someone is willing and able to own.
help.example: I can recruit five suitable sellers and organize interview notes. This is a proposed commitment, not completed work.
help.avoid: Avoid naming a skill without owning a concrete task.

questions.question: Which roles are missing from the team?
questions.rawQuestion: Which roles are missing from the team?
questions.sourceSection: 從 Idea 到 Problem：優勢、團隊與個人
questions.sourceRange:
來源：第二週第 31、35、37、43–45 頁。


三週是教材原本的反思期間；保留來源，不預設為未來網站的固定期限。

help.why: Gaps in the team become gaps in the work. Seeing them early lets you recruit, learn, or plan around them before they block progress.
help.example: The listing-data team might have product and engineering skills but no one comfortable selling to store owners. Write the roles the next three weeks need, mark who covers each, and circle the empty ones.
help.avoid: Avoid assuming someone will pick up a missing role later without naming who or when.

questions.question: Which role can I take responsibility for?
questions.rawQuestion: Which role can I take responsibility for?
questions.sourceSection: 從 Idea 到 Problem：優勢、團隊與個人
questions.sourceRange:
來源：第二週第 31、35、37、43–45 頁。


三週是教材原本的反思期間；保留來源，不預設為未來網站的固定期限。

help.why: Taking responsibility means owning a result, not just helping. Knowing what you can own makes it clear what the team can count on you for.
help.example: One founder might say she can own seller recruitment for the next three weeks, including outreach messages and scheduling. Write the role you will own and what done looks like for it.
help.avoid: Avoid offering to help with everything. Shared ownership of every task usually means nobody owns anything.

questions.question: Which role suits me best?
questions.rawQuestion: Which role suits me best?
questions.sourceSection: 從 Idea 到 Problem：優勢、團隊與個人
questions.sourceRange:
來源：第二週第 31、35、37、43–45 頁。


三週是教材原本的反思期間；保留來源，不預設為未來網站的固定期限。

help.why: The role you take on and the role that fits you best may differ. Fit affects how well and how long you can sustain the work.
help.example: In the listing-data team, a founder may be able to code but do her best work organizing interview evidence. Compare which tasks leave you energized after a long day and which drain you, and choose accordingly.
help.avoid: Avoid picking the role with the most impressive title instead of the one matching your real strengths.

questions.question: What kind of teammates am I looking for?
questions.rawQuestion: What kind of teammates am I looking for?
questions.sourceSection: 從 Idea 到 Problem：優勢、團隊與個人
questions.sourceRange:
來源：第二週第 31、35、37、43–45 頁。


三週是教材原本的反思期間；保留來源，不預設為未來網站的固定期限。

help.why: Knowing what you need in teammates makes recruiting deliberate. It also helps you notice when someone is pleasant but does not fill a real gap.
help.example: A founder of the listing-data venture might look for someone who can talk to store owners about budgets and is free for ten hours a week. Write the skills, availability, and attitude you need, in that order.
help.avoid: Avoid looking only for people who think and work exactly like you, which leaves the same gaps open.

questions.question: Do we have different but complementary skills?
questions.rawQuestion: Do we have different but complementary skills?
questions.sourceSection: 從 Problem 到 Team：合作
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第三週第 44–48 頁。

help.why: A team of similar people repeats the same blind spots. Complementary skills let the team cover research, building, and selling without overloading one person.
help.example: Put each founder's top two skills on a board. In the listing-data team, if everyone lists coding, the team lacks someone to interview sellers and someone to handle sales conversations.
help.avoid: Avoid counting difference alone as complementarity. Different skills only help if the work actually needs them.

questions.question: How will we divide the work?
questions.rawQuestion: How will we divide the work?
questions.sourceSection: 從 Problem 到 Team：分工、組隊驗證與第一次檢查
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第三週第 47–60 頁；標記轉問句的題目由職責或 Canvas 欄位展開。

help.why: Without an agreed split, some tasks are done twice and others not at all. A clear division makes progress visible and fair.
help.example: For a three-week sprint, the listing-data team could split work into seller interviews, market notes, and a manual pilot. Assign each to one owner, with a check-in date, and write it where everyone can see it.
help.avoid: Avoid dividing work only by who volunteers first in the meeting, without checking skills and available time.

questions.question: Who will research the problem and interview customers?
questions.rawQuestion: Who will research the problem and interview customers?（轉問句）
questions.sourceSection: 從 Problem 到 Team：分工、組隊驗證與第一次檢查
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第三週第 47–60 頁；標記轉問句的題目由職責或 Canvas 欄位展開。

help.why: Problem research and interviews produce the evidence every later decision depends on. Without a named owner, interviews get delayed or left unrecorded.
help.example: In the listing-data team, one founder could own finding sellers, scheduling calls, and keeping a shared interview log. Others join some calls, but she makes sure each one happens and is written up.
help.avoid: Avoid naming a whole team as owner. Pick one person accountable, even if several people help.

questions.question: Who will analyze the market?
questions.rawQuestion: Who will analyze the market?（轉問句）
questions.sourceSection: 從 Problem 到 Team：分工、組隊驗證與第一次檢查
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第三週第 47–60 頁；標記轉問句的題目由職責或 Canvas 欄位展開。

help.why: Market analysis tells you how many customers might have the problem and who else serves them. Someone needs to own this so it stays grounded.
help.example: For the listing-data venture, the market owner could list where small sellers gather, what tools they already use, and how many sellers fit the target description. Mark every figure as a source to check or an estimate.
help.avoid: Avoid assigning market analysis to whoever writes the pitch, which often turns it into impressive numbers without sources.

questions.question: Who will design and develop the product?
questions.rawQuestion: Who will design and develop the product?（轉問句）
questions.sourceSection: 從 Problem 到 Team：分工、組隊驗證與第一次檢查
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第三週第 47–60 頁；標記轉問句的題目由職責或 Canvas 欄位展開。

help.why: Design and development turn learning into something customers can try. A clear owner keeps the team from building before the problem is understood.
help.example: In the listing-data team, the engineer might own a small manual pilot first, such as a shared spreadsheet that fixes missing fields, before writing any software. She decides what gets built and when.
help.avoid: Avoid letting the builder start full development before interviews show what sellers actually need.

questions.question: Who will handle visual design and marketing communication?
questions.rawQuestion: Who will handle visual design and marketing communication?（轉問句）
questions.sourceSection: 從 Problem 到 Team：分工、組隊驗證與第一次檢查
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第三週第 47–60 頁；標記轉問句的題目由職責或 Canvas 欄位展開。

help.why: How the team presents itself affects whether sellers respond. Visual design and messaging need an owner so outreach and pitch materials stay consistent.
help.example: For the listing-data venture, one founder could own the outreach message, a simple one-page explanation of the pilot, and before-and-after listing samples. Track which wording gets more sellers to reply.
help.avoid: Avoid leaving visuals and messaging until the night before a pitch, when nobody has tested them with customers.

questions.question: Who will handle sales and business development?
questions.rawQuestion: Who will handle sales and business development?（轉問句）
questions.sourceSection: 從 Problem 到 Team：分工、組隊驗證與第一次檢查
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第三週第 47–60 頁；標記轉問句的題目由職責或 Canvas 欄位展開。

help.why: Someone must ask customers to commit, whether to a pilot, a payment, or an introduction. Without a sales owner, interest rarely turns into action.
help.example: In the listing-data team, the sales owner could follow up with interviewed sellers, propose a paid pilot, and find out who approves spending. She records each seller's response, including refusals.
help.avoid: Avoid assuming a good product will sell itself, or that sales can start only after the product is finished.

questions.question: Who will manage the project and communicate the proposal?
questions.rawQuestion: Who will manage the project and communicate the proposal?（轉問句）
questions.sourceSection: 從 Problem 到 Team：分工、組隊驗證與第一次檢查
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第三週第 47–60 頁；標記轉問句的題目由職責或 Canvas 欄位展開。

help.why: A project manager keeps deadlines, notes, and decisions in one place, and someone must present the proposal clearly to mentors, judges, or partners.
help.example: For the listing-data team, one founder could run weekly check-ins, keep the task board, and prepare the final proposal. She gathers evidence from others rather than writing every section herself.
help.avoid: Avoid giving this role to the person with the least other work, without checking they can communicate clearly.

questions.question: Are roles and owners clearly defined?
questions.rawQuestion: Are roles and owners clearly defined?
questions.sourceSection: 從 Problem 到 Team：分工、組隊驗證與第一次檢查
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第三週第 47–60 頁；標記轉問句的題目由職責或 Canvas 欄位展開。

help.why: Vague roles cause dropped tasks and quiet resentment. A clear owner for each role makes it easy to see who to ask and who is accountable.
help.example: Make a simple table for the listing-data team with each role, its owner, and its expected output this week. Ask every founder to read it back and confirm without changes.
help.avoid: Avoid stopping at a verbal agreement in a meeting. If it is not written, people remember it differently.

questions.question: Does every member have a specific task?
questions.rawQuestion: Does every member have a specific task?
questions.sourceSection: 從 Problem 到 Team：分工、組隊驗證與第一次檢查
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第三週第 47–60 頁；標記轉問句的題目由職責或 Canvas 欄位展開。

help.why: A member without a specific task drifts away or waits for direction. Concrete tasks keep everyone involved and make progress measurable.
help.example: In the listing-data team, a specific task could be interviewing three sellers by Friday or drafting the pilot offer by Wednesday. Check that each member's task has a deliverable and a date.
help.avoid: Avoid tasks like 'help with research' or 'support marketing', which cannot be checked at the end of the week.

questions.question: Who will invite customers, conduct interviews, and organize the evidence?
questions.rawQuestion: Who will invite customers, conduct interviews, and organize the evidence?
questions.sourceSection: Customer Validation & Growth：訪談與訪談後的檢查
questions.sourceRange:
來源：第四至五週第 25–26、30、39–40、45、47–49 頁。

直接問顧客：


團隊檢查：

help.why: Interviews involve several steps: finding people, talking to them, and turning notes into usable evidence. Each step can be skipped if no one owns it.
help.example: For the listing-data team, one founder could send invitations, a second could lead calls, and the third could tag notes by problem and seller type. Check after each round that all three steps were completed.
help.avoid: Avoid holding interviews without anyone owning the notes, which leaves evidence scattered across personal chats and memories.

questions.question: Who will update the customer profile and problem definition?
questions.rawQuestion: Who will update the customer profile and problem definition?
questions.sourceSection: Customer Validation & Growth：訪談與訪談後的檢查
questions.sourceRange:
來源：第四至五週第 25–26、30、39–40、45、47–49 頁。

直接問顧客：


團隊檢查：

help.why: Interviews only matter if they change the team's shared understanding. Someone must update the customer profile and problem statement when evidence shifts.
help.example: After a week of seller interviews, one founder could revise the target description, perhaps narrowing it to sellers who rely on supplier spreadsheets, and note which interviews prompted the change.
help.avoid: Avoid keeping the original customer profile because updating it feels like admitting a mistake.

questions.question: Who is on the team?
questions.rawQuestion: Who is on the team?
questions.sourceSection: Pitch 所需欄位轉問句
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第二週第 5 頁、第七週第 1 頁。這裡保留商業提問，刪除繳交及評分要求；這些題目由欄位轉寫，不是逐字問句。

help.why: Anyone reading a proposal wants to know who is actually doing the work. A clear list also shows the team who is committed and who is just interested.
help.example: For the listing-data venture, list each founder with one line on their background, such as a former small shop owner, an engineer, and a retail marketer. Include only people actively working now.
help.avoid: Avoid listing advisors or friends who gave one piece of advice as team members.

questions.question: What expertise and responsibilities does each member bring?
questions.rawQuestion: What expertise and responsibilities does each member bring?
questions.sourceSection: Pitch 所需欄位轉問句
questions.sourceRange: 來源：第二週第 5 頁、第七週第 1 頁。這裡保留商業提問，刪除繳交及評分要求；這些題目由欄位轉寫，不是逐字問句。

help.why: Readers of a pitch judge whether the team can deliver. Linking each person's expertise to a responsibility shows the team is organized, not just talented.
help.example: In the listing-data team, one founder brings experience running a small shop and owns seller interviews. Another has built import tools and owns the pilot. Pair each expertise with what that person is doing now.
help.avoid: Avoid listing impressive past credentials that have no connection to the current responsibilities.

questions.question: How much time is each person willing to commit each day?
questions.rawQuestion: How much time is each person willing to commit each day?
questions.sourceSection: 從 Idea 到 Problem：優勢、團隊與個人
questions.sourceRange:
來源：第二週第 31、35、37、43–45 頁。


三週是教材原本的反思期間；保留來源，不預設為未來網站的固定期限。

help.why: Daily time determines how fast the team can learn. Knowing each person's realistic daily hours prevents plans that quietly depend on one person.
help.example: In the listing-data team, one founder might give two hours each weekday evening, another only thirty minutes. Write the numbers down and plan tasks to fit the smallest realistic daily window.
help.avoid: Avoid answering with your best day. Use what you can sustain on an ordinary busy day.

questions.question: Are we willing to work in the evenings or on weekends?
questions.rawQuestion: Are we willing to work in the evenings or on weekends?
questions.sourceSection: 從 Idea 到 Problem：優勢、團隊與個人
questions.sourceRange:
來源：第二週第 31、35、37、43–45 頁。


三週是教材原本的反思期間；保留來源，不預設為未來網站的固定期限。

help.why: Many early teams work around jobs or classes. Agreeing whether evenings and weekends are in scope avoids surprise and resentment later.
help.example: The listing-data team could agree that weekday evenings are for async work and Saturday mornings are for joint interview reviews. Each person states which evenings or weekends they cannot give.
help.avoid: Avoid assuming everyone is available on weekends because one person is. Ask each member directly.

questions.question: How will the team make decisions?
questions.rawQuestion: How will the team make decisions?
questions.sourceSection: 從 Idea 到 Problem：優勢、團隊與個人
questions.sourceRange:
來源：第二週第 31、35、37、43–45 頁。


三週是教材原本的反思期間；保留來源，不預設為未來網站的固定期限。

help.why: Decisions will come up before anyone feels ready. Choosing a method early keeps disagreements from turning into delays or hurt feelings.
